title: Do Biased Models Have Biased Thoughts?
benchmark_measurement: Detection of bias and stereotypes in question-answering contexts related to religion, using the BBQ (Bias Benchmark for Question Answering) dataset. The analysis focused on whether a model's 'thoughts' (reasoning steps) and final outputs were biased when presented with scenarios involving religious topics.
findings: For the 'Religion' category, the correlation between biased thoughts and biased outputs was generally weak and often not statistically significant across the tested models. For example, the Pearson correlation was 0.23 for Llama8b, 0.17 for Phi, 0.10 for Gemma, 0.01 for Mistral, and -0.07 for Qwen. The statistical significance of this correlation varied, being high for Llama8b (p < 0.01) and moderate for Phi (p < 0.05), but insignificant for the other models.
